chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Haytham from Muhammad ibn Marwan said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Have your child nursed with the milk of a good (healthy/beautiful) woman, and beware of the bad (unhealthy/ugly) one, for the milk can transmit (qualities/diseases).'

key_terms.الْحِسَانِ: Good, healthy, or beautiful (referring to the wet nurse)
key_terms.وَالْقِبَاحَ: The bad, ugly, or unhealthy (referring to the wet nurse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on choosing a wet nurse based on health and character?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the profound impact of wet nursing on a child's physical and temperamental development, advising the selection of a healthy and virtuous nurse ('al-hisan') while avoiding those with defects ('al-qibah'). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'idha' (transmission), where the quality of milk is seen as a carrier of both bodily health and moral disposition, influencing the child's upbringing alongside biological lineage.
